# UIObject

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`
- **Abstract**: it cannot be created; other classes inherit from it

The base class of everything that occupies a rectangle in a UI tree. Its properties set where the rectangle is, how it is drawn, and how it responds to the pointer and to selection.

Positions and sizes are `UDim2` values: on each axis, a fraction of the parent plus an offset in pixels. That lets one layout work at every resolution.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AbsolutePosition` | `Vector2` | — | read-only | The position of the object's top left corner after layout, in window pixels. |
| `AbsoluteSize` | `Vector2` | — | read-only | The size of the object after layout, in window pixels. |
| `Active` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether the object receives the pointer: whether a press lands on it and whether the pointer counts as over it. A press on an active object belongs to the interface, which a game sees as `uiConsumed` in `InputService.InputBegan`. A press on an inactive object passes to whatever is under it and to the game.<br><br>Until you set it, the value depends on the class. A button, a `TextInput` and a `ScrollFrame` are active. A `TextLabel` and an `ImageLabel` are not, so a press on the icon or caption inside a button reaches the button. A `Frame` is active when it draws a background (`BackgroundTransparency` below 1), so a backdrop behind a dialog blocks what is under it, and a transparent frame used only for layout lets presses through.<br><br>Once you set it, your value is used: true on a transparent frame makes an invisible blocker, and false on a button makes it decorative. No object receives the pointer while `InputService.PointerLocked` is on. |
| `AnchorPoint` | `Vector2` | `Vector2.zero` | read/write | The point of this object that `Position` places, as a fraction of the object's own size. (0, 0) is its top left corner and (0.5, 0.5) is its center. |
| `AutomaticSize` | `Enum.AutomaticSize` | `Enum.AutomaticSize.None` | read/write | The axes on which the object sizes itself to fit its contents. On those axes, `Size` is ignored. |
| `BackgroundColor` | `Color3` | `Color3.new(1, 1, 1)` | read/write | The color of the fill behind the object's content. |
| `BackgroundTransparency` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How transparent the background is, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible). An object with an invisible background is still laid out; `Active` decides whether it receives the pointer. |
| `ClipsDescendants` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether descendants are clipped to this object's rectangle. A scrolling list needs it on; an object with a drop shadow outside its rectangle needs it off. |
| `LayoutOrder` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The position of this child in a `UIListLayout` whose `SortOrder` is `LayoutOrder`. It is ignored otherwise. |
| `NextSelectionDown` | `UIObject?` | — | read/write | The object that is selected when the selection moves down from this one. With nil, the nearest selectable object below it is chosen by position. |
| `NextSelectionLeft` | `UIObject?` | — | read/write | The object that is selected when the selection moves left from this one. With nil, the nearest selectable object to its left is chosen by position. |
| `NextSelectionRight` | `UIObject?` | — | read/write | The object that is selected when the selection moves right from this one. With nil, the nearest selectable object to its right is chosen by position. |
| `NextSelectionUp` | `UIObject?` | — | read/write | The object that is selected when the selection moves up from this one. With nil, the nearest selectable object above it is chosen by position. |
| `Position` | `UDim2` | `UDim2.new()` | read/write | The position of this object's `AnchorPoint` inside its parent. |
| `Rotation` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The rotation of the object, in degrees clockwise about its anchor point. It rotates how the object is drawn, not its layout: a rotated object still occupies its unrotated rectangle.<br><br>Descendants rotate with it, and a descendant's own `Rotation` is added. A dial rotated 30 degrees with a needle rotated 90 draws the needle at 120.<br><br>Rotation does not affect three things. Layout ignores it. Hit testing uses the unrotated rectangle. `ClipsDescendants` clips to an upright rectangle, so a rotated child of a clipping parent is clipped by the parent's unrotated box. |
| `Selectable` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether a gamepad or the arrow keys can select this object. Until you set it, the value depends on the class: a button and a `TextInput` are selectable, and nothing else is. The selected object is `UIService.SelectedObject`, and the gamepad's confirm button fires its `Activated`. |
| `SelectionImageObject` | `UIObject?` | — | read/write | An object drawn over this one while it is selected, in place of the default outline. Its background, image, corners, gradient and strokes are drawn at this object's rectangle. Its children are not drawn. |
| `Size` | `UDim2` | `UDim2.new()` | read/write | The size of the object: a fraction of its parent plus an offset. It is ignored on an axis that `AutomaticSize` covers. |
| `Visible` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this object and its descendants are laid out, drawn and able to receive the pointer. An invisible object does none of the three. |
| `ZIndex` | `number` | `0` | read/write | The drawing order within the `ScreenGui`: higher values are drawn later, on top. Objects with equal values are drawn in tree order. It does not affect layout, and it is one ordering across the whole tree, not one per parent. |

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `Activated()`

Fires when the object is activated: a pointer press and release both land on it, or the gamepad's confirm button is pressed while it is selected. A mouse click, a tap and a gamepad button all fire it.

### `PointerEntered()`

Fires when the pointer moves onto the object. The pointer is a mouse cursor or a finger.

### `PointerExited()`

Fires when the pointer moves off the object.

### `SelectionGained()`

Fires when the object becomes `UIService.SelectedObject`.

### `SelectionLost()`

Fires when the object stops being `UIService.SelectedObject`.
